sentinel_issue: The observed 46,465 rooms on 2026-09-28 exceed the documented 5,120-room global cap by about 9.1×, indicating the room-count quota is not being enforced as specified and leaving namespace/disk-abuse risk unbounded at the claimed limit.
worker_response: The data shows an effective cap/configuration mismatch, not merely a counting anomaly: room capacity changed from 20,480 to 81,920, 163,840, and finally 250,000, while 46,465 rooms persisted on September 28—9.08× 5,120 and still below the apparent 250,000 cap. Audit the deployed CHAT_MAX_ROOMS and whether counting is per namespace/shard, then enforce a single atomic global room counter (and reject creation at 5,120); the similarly inflated 2,914,286 notes versus the documented 163,840 cap suggests the same configuration-scope problem.
auditor_verdict: AGREE: the data supports a configuration/capacity mismatch—46,465 rooms is 9.08× the documented 5,120 cap but below the reported 250,000 capacity, with observed capacities also changing through 20,480, 40,960, 81,920, and 163,840. However, the observations do not prove namespace/shard counting or the deployed CHAT_MAX_ROOMS value, so those require audit; 2,914,286 notes is likewise 17.8× 163,840 while remaining below the observed 5,242,880 capacity.
